problems.comment:
Thus far only a little snow is lying. Individual avalanche prone locations are to be found in particular in extremely steep terrain at elevated altitudes. Even a snow slide can sweep people along and give rise to falls. 
 The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

bulletin.snowpack:
Snow cover
Snow depths are generally well below average for the time of year. Above around 2800 m, the deepest snow cover, ranging between 40 to 60 cm, can be found in Lower Valais, on the northern Alpine ridge from Diablerets to Titlis and in the Bernina region. In the other regions, the old snow cover is very thin and is in places contiguous, particularly on shady slopes above 2500m.
The snowpack contains widespread weak layers on high-altitude shady slopes. In areas where the snowpack is already contiguous and the terrain roughness is uniform, avalanches may be triggered in places within these weak layers of old snow.
bulletin.tendency:
Outlook
On Tuesday and Wednesday, there will be persistent and in places heavy precipitation in the west and north. The snowfall level will rise temporarily to around 2500 m on Tuesday and will be at 1800 m on Wednesday. From Monday to Wednesday evening, a widespread 30 bis 60 cm of fresh snow is to be expected in the high Alpine regions in Valais and on the northern Alpine ridge west of Titlis. In the extreme west of Lower Valais, up to 80 cm is possible in places. However, the amount of precipitation is still uncertain. On both days, the wind will be strong to storm-force, blowing from the west.
The avalanche danger will increase in all regions, and appreciably so in the regions exposed to heavier precipitation. Spontaneous dry avalanches are increasingly likely, especially in the high Alpine regions. With the rain, small wet snow avalanches are to be expected on Tuesday below 2500 m.

problems.comment:
10 to 20 cm of snow will fall until Monday above approximately 2200 m. 
 The westerly wind will transport the new snow. The fresh wind slabs will be deposited on a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes above approximately 2400 m. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches in some places, including medium-sized ones. 
 Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection. The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

problems.comment:
5 to 10 cm of snow fell on Sunday above approximately 2400 m. 20 to 40 cm of snow will fall until Monday above approximately 2200 m. 
 The westerly wind will transport the new snow. The fresh wind slabs will be deposited on a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes above approximately 2400 m. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches in some places. In many cases these are medium-sized. In the course of the day possibly danger level 3 (considerable) will be reached. 
 Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection. The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
